answer: Diminishing returns per operator: rewards are paid per independent operator, not per account. Accounts that share hosting, payout paths, timing patterns or near-identical prose are grouped, and each group's payout grows only with the square root of its seat count. Ten honest operators each earn a full share, while one operator running a hundred fakes earns about ten shares while paying for a hundred seats of work. Splitting a canyon of fakes into many small mesas just adds cost, so sybils stop paying long before the attacker sees any nectar.
